verified_features.evidence: A user-defined state schema plus nodes and edges forms a stateful workflow. Nodes may call an LLM or ordinary Python. Compile performs structural checks and configures runtime features.
verified_features.locator: Graph API: StateGraph; Compiling your graph; State

verified_features.evidence: Nodes return partial state updates. Each state key has a reducer; without a custom reducer an update replaces the previous value.
A routing function reads current state and returns destination node(s) or termination. Multiple outgoing static edges execute their destinations in the next parallel superstep.
LangGraph explicitly supports looping workflows, including routing back to the same/earlier node. It is not synonymous with a directed acyclic graph.
verified_features.locator: Graph API: opening overview and RemainingSteps examples

verified_features.evidence: A checkpointer saves within-thread execution state; a store supports application-defined data across threads. Persistence requires an appropriate backend and thread identity.
interrupt pauses for input; invoke with Command(resume=...) and the same thread_id. The interrupted node starts again from its beginning, re-executing code before the interrupt.
verified_features.locator: Interrupts: Pause using interrupt; Resuming interrupts; Rules of interrupts

verified_features.evidence: Use idempotent effects, move effects after interrupt or into separate nodes. A saved approval value is application data; authorization and engineering freshness checks remain application responsibilities.
verified_features.locator: Interrupts: Side effects called before interrupt must be idempotent; final sentence is engineering interpretation

langgraph.dag_definition: A directed acyclic graph has no directed cycle. A fixed one-attempt dependency plan may be a DAG even when its enclosing repair workflow is cyclic. A physical grid topology graph represents buses/lines, not execution order.
langgraph.illustrative_dag: Freeze case → AC power flow → selected contingency branches in parallel → aggregate violations → report
langgraph.illustrative_conditional_workflow: Candidate → numerical solve → deterministic limit/requirements checks; pass → operator review; fail with budget → repair → solve; invalid input or budget exhausted → stop
do_not_claim: A compiled graph proves physics correctness.
A checkpoint proves the case is fresh.
A human interrupt alone grants authority to actuate.
The reviewed E01–E04 papers use LangGraph unless separately documented.

recommended_selection: Use E01 for MCP decomposition/numeric retrieval, E02 for execution-feedback versus semantic correctness, E03 for state/validation/rollback architecture, E04 for an explicit same-model no-tool/tool comparison. These complement existing R01/R02/P01–P04 rather than replace numerical-solvers or become field-deployment proof.
plotting_rules: No cross-paper ranking: tasks and metrics differ.
Show named study setup and exact metric on every result chart.
Do not infer missing denominators for E03 or confidence intervals for E02 graded scores.
For E04 show counts out of150 and single-feeder caveat; repeat-run uncertainty is unspecified.
Reproduced values are author-reported. Original diagrams explain architecture; they are not reproduced experimental data.
